name: Higashi-Jujo
tagline: Shinjuku in 23 minutes and Tokyo in 25 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000.
summary: The station is in Kita City, where JR East run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 29 minutes to Otemachi, 23 minutes to Shinjuku, 28 minutes to Shibuya and 39 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. The station stands 8.3 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 18.8 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 8.3 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 4 m to 22.8 m, a difference of 18.8 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 5 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 3 to 5 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is about average for the 23 wards.

groceries.name: サミット 王子桜田通り店

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 23 clinics and 26 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 明理会中央総合病院, about 4 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 八木病院, about 6 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: JR Keihin-Tohoku Line.
congestion: JR Keihin-Tohoku Line runs at 159% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 大井町→品川, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥70,000 to ¥80,000 and 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000. 1LDK ¥150,000 to ¥160,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥70,000 to ¥80,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the low side. What holds the figure down: only one line, the {line}, serving the station. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: Higashi-Jujo is ahead on how easy the shopping is, and little else separates the two.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Higashi-Jujo. Higashi-Jujo adds the JR Keihin-Tohoku Line; Jujo adds the JR Saikyo Line. Which is faster depends on where you are going: Higashi-Jujo is 5 minutes quicker to Tokyo, Jujo is 11 minutes quicker to Roppongi. On how easy the shopping is, Higashi-Jujo comes out ahead. Within about 13 minutes' walk, Higashi-Jujo has 14 supermarkets (The and みらべる and others) and Jujo has 9.

neighbours.lead: Higashi-Jujo is ahead on how close the centre is and lower rent.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Higashi-Jujo. Higashi-Jujo adds the JR Keihin-Tohoku Line; Oji-Kamiya adds the Tokyo Metro Namboku Line. Higashi-Jujo is at least 9 minutes quicker to Shibuya and Shinjuku. A one-room flat also costs about ¥12,000 more at Oji-Kamiya.

goodFor: People who want to finish their shopping on foot
People living alone who want to hold the rent down
notFor: People who want another route when service is suspended
noiseSources: 中十条赤羽線 (1 lanes each way) runs just outside the station. In a flat facing it, the cars are audible morning and evening

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 14 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 3 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: Only the JR Keihin-Tohoku Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the low side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Mornings here are less crowded than the line figures suggest: the lines are busy, but this station is outside their busiest stretches.
leads.noiseSources: Whether a flat faces the road changes what you hear indoors.
